tools.name: search_statutes
tools.description:
Search North Carolina (NC) statutes by topic, keyword or phrase.

Use this when you know the SUBJECT but not the citation — "what's the NC law about
leaving a dog in a hot car", "failure to appear penalty", "when can I expunge a
misdemeanor". If you already have a citation, use get_statute instead.

tools.name: get_statute
tools.description:
Full text of one North Carolina (NC) General Statutes section, by citation.

Use for "what does G.S. 14-72.1 say". Accepts any spelling — "14-72.1", "G.S. 14-72.1",
"§ 14-72.1". Returns catchline, body, history note, and when it was first enacted and
last amended. `as_of` gives the text observed on

tools.name: pending_changes
tools.description:
North Carolina (NC) statute text already enacted but not yet effective.

Use for "what changes to Chapter 14 are coming". Returns each section's current text
alongside the future variant, its effective date, and by default a diff of the two.
Distinguishes an AMENDMENT (current text exists) from a NE

tools.name: amendment_history
tools.description:
When a North Carolina (NC) statute section was enacted and every time it was amended.

Use for "how often has G.S. 14-33 changed" or "when was this last amended". Returns one
entry per session law mined from the section's own history note, grouped by year, plus
first-enacted year and total amendment

tools.name: diff_statute
tools.description:
Word-level diff of a North Carolina (NC) statute section between two versions.

`mode="pending"` compares the text in force against an enacted-but-not-yet-effective
variant — use this for "what will change on 1 October". `mode="observed"` compares
versions this database has actually recorded, option

so it also answers "what takes effect n

tools.description:

Use for "which parts of Chapter 14 keep changing". Returns amendment counts by year,
the most-amended sections with their totals, and counts of pending and repealed
sections. Omit `chapter` for a corpus-wide view.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "get_statute" stacks urgency/override words (never, override). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: rule_history · Private data: get_statute, amendment_history, diff_statute, recent_law_changes, search_rules · Public sink: recent_law_changes · Destructive: get_statute, rule_history.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: rule_history · Private data: get_statute, amendment_history, diff_statute, recent_law_changes, search_rules · Public sink: recent_law_changes · Destructive: get_statute, rule_history

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_statutes" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
